groups.name: Acyl Halides & Acid Chlorides
groups.description: Highly reactive organic acid halides (e.g., Sebacoyl chloride, Thionyl chloride) that undergo violent nucleophilic acyl substitution and moisture hydrolysis.

groups.name: Halogenated Organic Compounds
groups.description: Chlorinated/brominated hydrocarbons (e.g., Dichloromethane, Chloroform) sensitive to active metals and caustics; persistent environmental toxins.

groups.name: Water-Reactive Substances
groups.description: Substances (e.g., NaBH4, LiAlH4, TDI, Sebacoyl chloride) that react violently with moisture, generating explosive H2 or choking acid mists.

groups.name: Water & Aqueous Solutions
groups.description: Water, aqueous buffers, saline, scrubber waters, and water-based chemical formulations.

groups.name: Strong Oxidizing Agents
groups.description: Electron acceptors (e.g., Nitric acid 68%, Hydrogen peroxide 50%, Sodium hypochlorite, KMnO4) capable of causing runaway combustion with organics.

groups.name: General Oxidizing Agents
groups.description: Oxidizing compounds capable of accelerating combustion and oxidizing multivalent transition metals.

groups.name: Strong Reducing Agents & Hydrides
groups.description: Substances (e.g., Sodium borohydride, Lithium aluminum hydride) that release flammable hydrogen gas or react violently with oxidizers.

groups.name: General Reducing Agents
groups.description: Mild reducing compounds and oxidizable multivalent salts (e.g., Basic Chromium Sulfate, Sulfites).

groups.name: Inorganic / Mineral Acids
groups.description: Strong mineral acids (e.g., Sulfuric acid 98%, Hydrochloric acid 35%, Nitric acid 68%, Phosphoric acid 85%) that violently neutralize bases and protonate sulfides.

groups.name: Organic / Carboxylic Acids
groups.description: Carbon-based acids (e.g., Formic acid, Glacial acetic acid, Glycolic acid, Salicylic acid) that react exothermically with bases and protonate sulfides.

groups.name: Caustics & Strong Alkaline Bases
groups.description: Alkaline compounds (e.g., Sodium hydroxide 50%, Calcium hydroxide lime, Sodium carbonate, Ammonia) that react violently with acids.

groups.name: Alcohols & Polyols
groups.description: Hydroxy compounds (e.g., Isopropanol, Methanol, Ethanol, Phenoxyethanol) susceptible to rapid esterification and flammability.

groups.name: Aliphatic Amines & Organic Bases
groups.description: Organic amines (e.g., Triethylamine, Ammonium hydroxide) acting as strong nucleophiles.

groups.name: Cyanides & Nitriles
groups.description: Cyanide salts and organic nitriles (e.g., Acetonitrile) capable of releasing lethal Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) gas under acidic conditions.

groups.name: Sulfides & Hydrosulfides
groups.description: Inorganic/organic sulfides (e.g., Sodium sulfide Na2S, Sodium hydrosulfide NaHS) that release instantaneous lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) gas upon contact with acids.

groups.name: Organic Peroxides
groups.description: Unstable O-O bond organic peroxides (e.g., Benzoyl peroxide 75%) prone to thermal runaway, explosive decomposition, and violent deflagration.

groups.name: Inorganic Peroxides
groups.description: Hydrogen peroxide solutions prone to catalytic decomposition, violent oxidation, and steam overpressurization.

groups.name: Flammable & Combustible Solvents
groups.description: Low-flashpoint organic solvents (e.g., Isopropanol, Ethanol, THF, Limonene, Ethyl acetate) presenting severe vapor fire hazards.

groups.name: Aliphatic & Terpene Hydrocarbons
groups.description: Volatile fragrance terpenes and aliphatic hydrocarbons (e.g., Limonene) susceptible to rapid auto-oxidation and peroxide formation.

groups.name: Isocyanates
groups.description: Organic isocyanates (e.g., Toluene diisocyanate TDI) that react with water, amines, and bases with violent gas evolution and polymerization.

groups.name: Cytotoxic & Antineoplastic Agents
groups.description: Genotoxic, mutagenic, or teratogenic antineoplastic pharmaceuticals (e.g., Cisplatin, Methotrexate) governed by USP <800>.

groups.name: Quaternary Ammonium Compounds
groups.description: Cationic conditioning surfactants (e.g., Cetrimonium chloride) incompatible with anionic detergents.

groups.name: Anionic Surfactants
groups.description: Sulfated/sulfonated anionic surfactants (e.g., Sodium laureth sulfate SLES).

groups.name: Aldehydes
groups.description: Carbonyl compounds (e.g., Formaldehyde 37%) that polymerize exothermically with acids and react with oxidizers.

groups.name: Peroxidizable Ethers
groups.description: Volatile ethers (e.g., Tetrahydrofuran THF) prone to explosive auto-peroxidation on air exposure.

groups.name: Neutral Salts & Minerals
groups.description: Inorganic sulfates, chlorides, and minerals without direct explosive cross-reactivity.

matrix.hazardTitle: FATAL ACCIDENT HAZARD: Instantaneous Lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Gas Release
matrix.description: Contact between inorganic sulfides (Sodium sulfide, NaHS) and mineral acids (Sulfuric, Hydrochloric, Nitric, Phosphoric) causes instantaneous liberation of lethal, asphyxiating Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) gas. H2S causes rapid olfactory nerve paralysis, pulmonary edema, and sudden collapse/death within 1-2 breaths at >500 ppm.
matrix.segregationAction: MANDATORY ISOLATION: Store in separate dedicated bays with minimum 6 meters physical distance or a 1-hour fire-rated barrier. Sulfide stores must have continuous H2S sensors interlocking to emergency caustic scrubbers. NEVER co-mingle wastewater streams.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Evacuate area immediately upwind. Wear positive-pressure SCBA. Neutralize spills strictly with alkaline oxidizing bleach solution (pH > 11), NEVER with acid.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 / Tannery Safety Directive

matrix.hazardTitle: Lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Gas Generation via Organic Acid Protonation
matrix.description: Organic carboxylic acids (Formic acid, Glacial acetic acid, Glycolic acid) rapidly protonate sulfide salts, releasing toxic H2S gas and flammable organic fumes. Common fatal occurrence during leather pickling or deliming if liming liquor residue is present in drums.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate organic acids in an acid-proof chemical store physically separated from sodium sulfide and liming chemical pallets.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Monitor air with portable multi-gas detector. Ensure continuous ventilation in leather drum unloading bays.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / Leather Technologists & Chemists Association Guide

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Exothermic Oxidation, Flash Fire & Toxic Sulfur Dioxide Cloud
matrix.chemicalEquation: Na2S + 4 H2O2 -> Na2SO4 + 4 H2O + Extreme Heat
matrix.description: Mixing solid sulfides with strong oxidizers (Hydrogen peroxide, Nitric acid, Sodium hypochlorite, KMnO4) produces an extremely violent exothermic redox reaction capable of boiling solutions, erupting corrosive liquid spray, and releasing toxic SO2 and H2S gases.
matrix.segregationAction: Store sulfides in dedicated alkaline bay at least 8 meters away from oxidizer bunkers.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Flood with massive water deluge from safe distance. Wear full chemical splash suit and SCBA.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / NFPA 400 Hazardous Materials Code

matrix.hazardTitle: Auto-Ignition, Runaway Deflagration & Severe Industrial Fire
matrix.chemicalEquation: Oxidizer + Flammable Solvent -> CO2 + H2O + Spontaneous Thermal Explosion
matrix.description: Strong oxidizers (Nitric acid 68%, H2O2 50%, Sodium hypochlorite, KMnO4) react exothermically with low-flashpoint flammable solvents (IPA, Ethanol, Methanol, THF, Ethyl acetate, Limonene). Vapors auto-ignite spontaneously causing devastating warehouse fires.
matrix.segregationAction: NFPA 400 MANDATE: Minimum 20 feet (6.1 meters) separation distance or a 1-hour fire-rated barrier wall between Class 5.1 oxidizers and Class 3 flammable liquids.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Use foam/water fog suppression. Eliminate all potential electrical and mechanical ignition sources.

matrix.description: In cosmetic manufacturing warehouses, storing concentrated bulk Hydrogen peroxide adjacent to fragrance terpenes (Limonene, Linalool) creates an extreme auto-oxidation hazard. Terpenes form unstable cyclic peroxides that detonate under mild heat.
matrix.segregationAction: Store concentrated hydrogen peroxide in an isolated cold-storage bunker (< 20°C) with self-venting caps. Fragrance terpenes must reside in a separate flame-proof solvent room.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Cool drum exteriors with water spray. Evacuate warehouse immediately if temperature rise is detected.
matrix.authoritativeSource: Cosmetics Industry Safety Consortium / NOAA CAMEO

matrix.incompatibilityType: Chemical Reactivity & Toxic Hexavalent Chromium Formation
matrix.hazardTitle: Hazardous Cr(VI) Oxidation & Violent Redox Exotherm
matrix.chemicalEquation: 2 Cr(OH)SO4 + 3 H2O2 + 4 NaOH -> 2 Na2CrO4 (Cr VI) + 2 Na2SO4 + 8 H2O
matrix.description: Mixing Basic Chromium Sulfate Cr(III) with strong oxidizers (Hydrogen peroxide, Bleach, Nitric acid) oxidizes benign trivalent chromium into Carcinogenic, Mutagenic Hexavalent Chromium Cr(VI). A critical environmental and biological contamination risk.
matrix.segregationAction: Strictly segregate chromium tanning powders from oxidizer bunkers. Never co-mingle wastewater before chrome precipitation recovery is complete.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Treat any accidental cross-mix with reducing agents (Sodium bisulfite, FeSO4) at pH < 3 to reduce Cr(VI) back to Cr(III).
matrix.authoritativeSource: Leather Working Group (LWG) Chemical Management Standard / EPA

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Hydrogen (H2) Gas Explosion & Flash Fire
matrix.chemicalEquation: NaBH4 + 4 H2O -> NaB(OH)4 + 4 H2(g) ^ + Rapid Exotherm
matrix.description: Hydride reducing agents (Sodium borohydride, Lithium aluminum hydride) react violently upon contact with water, steam, or aqueous moisture, evolving large volumes of explosive Hydrogen gas and generating intense heat that ignites the gas.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in hermetically sealed metal drums under dry nitrogen blanket in an isolated moisture-free room. Prohibit fire sprinkler water in hydride storage rooms (Class D powder only).
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: NEVER use water or CO2 fire extinguishers. Smother fires exclusively with Class D dry powder (Met-L-X or dry sodium chloride).

matrix.hazardTitle: Explosive Hydrogen Blast & Corrosive Mist Eruption
matrix.description: Contact between hydrides and mineral acids causes an instantaneous, explosive burst of hydrogen and potentially toxic borane gases, blowing out reactor vessel relief discs.
matrix.segregationAction: Physically isolate hydrides from all acid drum storage by at least 10 meters.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Evacuate area immediately. Shut off master electrical feeds to prevent ignition of hydrogen cloud.
matrix.authoritativeSource: Bretherick's Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards / NOAA CAMEO

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Hydrolysis, Pressure Blowout & Choking HCl Acid Release
matrix.description: Acyl halides (Sebacoyl chloride, Thionyl chloride) react violently with water or moisture, releasing dense plumes of choking Hydrogen Chloride (HCl) gas and rapidly overpressurizing closed drums.
matrix.segregationAction: Store under dry inert gas with airtight desiccant caps. Isolate from aqueous storage tanks.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Wear acid-gas respirator or SCBA. Vent reactor vessel only into caustic scrubbers.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / ACS Chemical Safety Manual

matrix.hazardTitle: Runaway Exotherm & Corrosive Hot Liquid Splattering
matrix.chemicalEquation: R-COCl + NaOH -> R-COONa + NaCl + Boiling Steam
matrix.description: Direct mixing of concentrated acid halides with strong caustic lye causes instantaneous thermal runaway, explosive boiling, and violent expulsion of caustic/acidic liquid.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in separate cabinets. Neutralization must be carried out only in controlled jacketed batch reactors with chilled diluent.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Wear full acid-suit with face shield. Flood eye wash immediately if exposed.

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Exothermic Neutralization & Boiling Corrosive Spray
matrix.chemicalEquation: H2SO4 + 2 NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2 H2O + Delta H (-114 kJ/mol)
matrix.description: Mixing concentrated mineral acids (H2SO4 98%, HCl 35%, HNO3 68%) with concentrated caustic lye (NaOH 50%, Ca(OH)2) releases immense heat instantly, converting water into superheated steam that erupts boiling corrosive liquid.
matrix.segregationAction: MANDATORY SEPARATION: Class 8A (Acids) and Class 8B (Bases) must NEVER share the same secondary containment bund or drainage trench.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Never pour water or base into concentrated acid. Always add acid slowly to water with continuous mechanical cooling.

matrix.hazardTitle: Rapid Evolution of Lethal Yellow-Green Chlorine Gas (Cl2)
matrix.description: Mixing industrial hypochlorite bleach (NaClO 12.5%) with hydrochloric acid instantly liberates dense clouds of suffocating Chlorine gas. Cl2 causes severe pulmonary edema, fluid accumulation in lungs, and chemical asphyxiation.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate bleach from all mineral acids with physical partition and dedicated spill collection trays.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Evacuate crosswind and upwind. Wear Level A/B hazmat suit with SCBA.
matrix.authoritativeSource: EPA Chemical Emergency Preparedness Advisory / NOAA CAMEO

matrix.hazardTitle: Lethal Chloramine Gas Release & Nitrogen Trichloride Explosion
matrix.description: Mixing bleach with ammonia or aliphatic amines (Triethylamine) generates toxic Chloramine (NH2Cl) vapors and shock-sensitive explosive Nitrogen Trichloride (NCl3).
matrix.segregationAction: Store ammonia and amine drums in separate storage zones away from bleach and peroxides.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Ventilate area thoroughly with spark-proof exhaust fans.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / NIOSH Pocket Guide

matrix.hazardTitle: Severe Drum Overpressurization & Catastrophic Vessel Rupture
matrix.description: Isocyanates (TDI) react exothermically with water and atmospheric moisture, releasing high-pressure Carbon Dioxide gas. In sealed drums, this builds pressure rapidly causing catastrophic drum blowout.
matrix.segregationAction: Maintain airtight dry nitrogen blankets on all isocyanate storage tanks. Ensure desiccant breathers on bulk tanks are checked weekly.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Never seal a drum contaminated with water. Decontaminate with liquid surfactant/alcohol/ammonia neutralizer solution.
matrix.authoritativeSource: International Isocyanate Institute Safety Manual / NOAA CAMEO

matrix.chemicalEquation: Organic Peroxide (BPO) + Solvent -> Rapid Free-Radical Deflagration
matrix.description: Organic peroxides (Benzoyl peroxide) are strong oxidizers with low thermal stability. Mixing with flammable solvents causes accelerated free-radical decomposition and violent detonation.
matrix.segregationAction: Store organic peroxides in dedicated isolated refrigerated bunker away from all flammable solvents.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Maintain water wetting in benzoyl peroxide. Keep temperature strictly below Self-Accelerating Decomposition Temperature (SADT 55°C).

matrix.description: Halogenated solvents (Dichloromethane, Chloroform) react exothermically with concentrated caustics or strong bases, forming explosive chloroacetylenes or hazardous phosgene traces.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in dedicated Halogenated Solvent bay away from caustic soda drums.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Never use caustic scrubbers directly on concentrated chlorinated solvent vapors without dilution.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / EPA Solvents Guide

matrix.hazardTitle: Complex Coacervation, Phase Inversion & Insoluble Sludge Formation
matrix.chemicalEquation: Cationic (CTAC) + Anionic (SLES) -> Insoluble Coacervate Salt Precipitate
matrix.description: Cationic surfactants react with anionic surfactants to form thick insoluble curds, plugging process transfer pumps, heat exchangers, and pipe manifolds.
matrix.segregationAction: Physically isolate cationic and anionic bulk storage drums to avoid mixing during raw material charging.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Flush fouled lines with hot isopropanol or non-ionic surfactant solution.
